 A for loop for calculating and printing the cube of each number from 1 to 20
 
```{r}
for (i in seq_len(20)) {print(i^3)}
```
for loop generating random 5 letter character 

```{r}
for (i in seq_len(5)) {
  print(paste(sample(letters, 5, replace = TRUE), collapse = ""))
}
```
using for loops to do things to each item in a vector
```{r}
library(cowsay)
species <- c("frog", "stegosaurus", "squirrel", "ghost")

for (spp in species) {
  say(paste("I am a", spp), by = spp)
}
```
```{r}
species <- c("monkey", "shark", "turkey", "snowman")

for (spp in species) {
  has_s <- startsWith(spp, "s")
  say(paste("Do I start with an s?", has_s), by = spp)
}
```
remember everything inside {} is the looped code

choosing a random 10-course rbeakfast using for loops and sample() function from a vector 

```{r}
breakfast <- c("eggs", "bacon", "sausages", "toast")
nums <- seq_len(5)

break_df <- tibble()

for (i in seq_len(10)) { item <- sample(breakfast, size = 1)
num <- sample(nums, size = 1)
row <- tibble(
  item = item,
  count = num
)
break_df <- bind_rows(break_df, row)}
gt(break_df)

```

## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this 

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
